newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains approves share buyback program.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains approves share buyback program.

text.p: Earthgrains Co said Monday its board of directors authorized a program to allow the company to repurchase up to 500,000 shares of its common stock, or about five percent of its outstanding shares.

The program is subject to a tax ruling by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, confirming it will not affect the company's tax-free spinoff from Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc. Earthgrains said it expects a favorable tax ruling in the near future.
The repurchased shares would be available for use under Earthgrains' employee benefit programs and for other general corporate purposes, the company said.
The program authorization extends through the end of calendar year 2000. Earthgrains said it would repurchase shares in the open market through J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.

"While our priorities for cash continue to be focused on reinvestment in our business and participation in industry consolidation, this authorization gives Earthgrains the additional alternative of repurchasing shares to enhance shareholder value," Barry Beracha, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
Earthgrains produces fresh-baked goods and refrigerated dough products.
